prompts:
Write the short overview a person reads at the top of their Memory page: what is remembered about them, as one paragraph.
Write the paragraph in English.
Use that language's own everyday words: translate any term in the entries into it, but keep every name exactly as written, accents included. Copy no word from another language out of an entry, however common it has become (it is spelt the way that other language spells it): write this language's own everyday word for the same thing, and keep the borrowed word only when there is none.
Use only the entries given. Do not add, guess or generalise beyond them, and leave out what they do not say. Keep each detail with the entry it comes from: never move a time, place, name or number to another entry, and keep what is being learned, planned or looked for as learning, planning or looking.
An entry marked ongoing is under way now and one marked temporary is a passing state; present nothing as finished or past unless an entry says so.
Refer to the person by their name, in the third person, when a name is given; otherwise address them as you.
Cover every subject the entries are filed under, with at least one short, plain sentence for each, and leave no entry out: when a subject has several small entries, name each in a few words within one sentence rather than dropping any. Use as many sentences as that takes, never more than ten, each one simple, with no fact twice; no headings, lists, quotation marks or emphasis. Never mention memory, entries, lists or this task.
Return JSON: {"overview": "<the paragraph>"}.

results.text: Kata is a thirty-five-year-old vegetarian freelance graphic designer whose native language is Hungarian and who speaks English fluently. She is currently working on a bookshop's brand identity, must hand in a logo design to a client by Friday, and is studying part-time for a master's degree expected to be completed next June. Kata lives in a two-room flat in Győr, having moved from Szeged where her younger brother Bence still lives, and is looking for a new flat because the current one is too small. She shares her home with her partner Márk, who is a teacher, their four-year-old daughter Lili, and a cat named Mák. Her mother-in-law will stay with them for two days next week. In her free time, Kata bakes sourdough bread, hikes in the Bakony, and goes bouldering twice a week at a local gym. She is learning Japanese with weekly lessons, learning to play the ukulele, and building a garden shed in her grandparents' garden. She enjoys reading science fiction novels by Ursula K. Le Guin and drinks black coffee without sugar. Kata is lactose intolerant, wears glasses for short-sightedness, and is currently attending physiotherapy for an injured knee. She is not drinking alcohol this week, plans a trip to Lisbon with Márk in March, and prefers written messages over phone calls for short, direct communication.

The Garden hut project aims to build a wooden structure for storing tools and garden furniture in the north corner of the garden. Kata and her father work on it together, while Kata's uncle, Péter, poured the concrete foundation. The floor area is 12 square metres, and timber was ordered from a local sawmill for 180 thousand forints. The foundation is finished and the wall frame is being built, with roofing sheets arriving next week. The roof will have a single pitch with a gentle slope, and the door will be a double door that opens outwards. The paint colour is not decided yet and will be chosen later.
